rhythm.value: Detector: 4 shots, median 4.0 s, 3 cuts. Corrected: 10 shots, 9 cuts (4 hard cuts, 2 text swaps on a held ground, then after 14.5 s two fades through the empty light ground and one dissolve), median 1.6 s, about 24 changes per minute; the longest hold is the interface at 5.9 s. Music-led, no voice. Sound was not heard: every sound statement comes from audio.json, audiomap.json and my own band-split envelope of the media. audio.json reads 93.27 BPM (confidence 0.61, downbeat confidence 0.03); that is a 2:3 artefact of a syncopated pattern (93.27 x 1.5 = 139.9). audiomap.json reads 139.98 BPM, grid reliable (0.72), but its beat phase sits on the off-beats: its beats (3.828, 4.255, ...) are 0.19 s before the kick-led beats. The six intro hits (0.140, 0.893, 1.532, 1.856, 2.499, 3.572 s, full-band swells) fall exactly 36, 29, 23, 20, 14 and 4 sixteenths before 4.000 s (sixteenth = 0.10714 s, error under 5 ms), so the true grid is beat k at 4.000 + 0.42857 k s. On that grid all six structural changes in 0-14.5 s land within 24 ms of a beat: 2.283 (beat -4, -3 ms), 4.000 (beat 0), 5.283 (beat 3, -3 ms), 6.150 (beat 5, +7 ms), 7.433 (beat 8, +4 ms), 10.017 (beat 14, +17 ms), each placed on its step-1 strip frame. Chance at +-0.03 s is 14% per change; one of the six fixed the phase, so five independent hits at 14% is about 5e-5. sync.json's cutsOnBeatRatio 0 against chance 0.231 is void: it uses the 93 BPM grid and only 3 detector cuts. Onsets are too dense (about 5.4 per second in 0-15 s) for cutsOnOnsetRatio 1.0 against 0.734 chance to mean anything. Holds within a state are 1-3 beats; every state ends with a one-beat accelerating exit that starts on a hit.

purpose.value: Hook in two sentences on white: what launched (with inline partner icons), then the scale in accent-coloured numbers. Corrected into two shots by the cut at 2.283 s.

technique.value: Two-line block laid out in its final position, left edge fixed at 11.5% width; each word appears whole on one frame every 8 source frames (0.133 s) while the block rises 8.5% of height with an ease-out over 12 frames at 30 fps; six icons fade and scale in one after another inside the second line. Exit: the whole block accelerates upward 7-8% of height over one beat (ease-in), then a hard cut.
evidence: visuals/a1/hook-words.jpg F8, F16, F24, F34, F42-F47

purpose.value: The drop: hard cut to a full orange ground with a hero percentage at about 90% of frame width.

technique.value: Ground swap on the downbeat with no flash, ring or echo. The number carries on the upward drift of the previous exit (7.5% of height, ease-out, 12 frames at 30 fps), then on the next beat shrinks from 89.5% to 35% width with heavy motion blur.

purpose.value: Finish the claim on the same orange: the comparison line, then the qualifier with a small subline.

technique.value: The number re-grows for half a beat (6 frames) and is swapped on the beat for the line, which enters at 67% width and eases out to 81%. Two beats later a second swap to a shorter, bigger line at 48% growing to 60.5% width, subline 4 frames later. Exit: the line grows to 77% with motion blur over 10 frames into a hard cut to white.

purpose.value: Product in use, then proof of scale and the brand: prompt bar types a request, the chat answers with a table, the camera reads it and scrolls; a line about sources; a chip wall; one chip picked; the logo; hard stop. Corrected into 5 shots.

technique.value: Real interface at reading scale, built up in place. A cursor clicks send and the frame is perfectly still for 0.58 s (F566-F600) before the cut, so the click reads before the answer. The answer streams in, table rows add downward, the camera drifts up and right with acceleration, then a fast vertical scroll with strong blur is sharp again by the downbeat at 14.286 s and settles by 14.75 s.

value.name: accelerate-into-cut
value.description: One-beat accelerating exit into a ground swap on the drop. The white stat block starts rising on the hit one beat before the drop (3.572 s) and accelerates 7.8% of height over 0.4 s (24 frames at 60 fps); at exactly 4.000 s the frame becomes orange with the hero number already at 90% width, still drifting upward and decelerating. The motion continues across the cut while colour and scale jump. The same exit closes every state before 7.5 s: F113-F136 into the cut at 2.283 s (diff rising linearly 0.3 to 5.8, quad-in), F214-F238 into 4.000 s, and F424-F444 into 7.433 s (diff rising 0.1 to 7.7, steeper at the end: expo-in, with blur on the last frames). Frame numbers at the source's 60 fps.
value.why: The eye is already travelling upward when the cut hits, so the cut feels like the music pulling the picture rather than a slide change; the drift continues on the far side, which hides the seam and makes the ground swap the only event.

evidence: own envelope: full-band swell 4.006 s, low band 4.021 s

value.name: hero-word-blur-shrink
value.description: Hero number shrinks with motion blur on beat 1 after the drop: 89.5% to 44% width in 8 frames at 30 fps, then eases to 35% by frame 152; re-grows for 6 frames and is swapped on beat 3. Strip at 60 fps: the shrink starts at F265 (4.417 s, diff 5.1), peaks F270-F271 (10.2) and decays by half about every 4 frames to under 1 by F284 (expo-out); the re-grow F307-F314 accelerates into the swap at F317 (5.283 s).
value.why: The number lands huge on the drop, then gives room for the sentence that explains it; the shrink with blur reads as physical speed, and the re-grow builds pressure into the next swap.

value.name: fixed-layout-word-build
value.description: Sentence revealed word by word in its final layout: the block is laid out first and never reflows (both lines centred on x 0.50 per the OCR boxes; the first line's left edge stays at 10.5% of width), words switch on whole at F8, F16, F24 and F34 (60 fps), about every 0.133-0.167 s, inline brand icons stagger in at about 2 frames apart inside the second line, and the whole block rises and settles once.
value.why: Laying the full sentence out first means nothing reflows as words arrive, so the eye reads left to right without being dragged; the icons are words, which says 'works with everything' without a logo wall.

value.name: click-freeze-cut
value.description: Click, freeze, cut. The cursor glides to the send button while the last words still type (arrives about F553, 9.22 s; typing ends about F563), then the frame is perfectly still (diff 0.00) for 35 frames, F566-F600 (0.58 s), until the hard cut at F601 (10.017 s, beat 14 on the corrected grid) to the chat window, which rises from below.
value.why: Stillness before the cut lets the click register as the cause; the answer then arrives as the effect on the beat.

value.name: blur-scroll-landing
value.description: Camera reads the real table, accelerates, and scrolls fast with heavy vertical blur (13.0-14.0 s; blurred rows F822-F840 at 60 fps). From F842 (14.03 s) the rows are sharp again while still travelling, OCR reads them from 14.10-14.27 s, so they are legible on the downbeat at 14.286 s; the travel then decelerates (diff 6.9 at F865 halving to under 1 by F883) and stops at F885 (14.75 s).
value.why: Speed shows volume without a number; the rows turning sharp on the downbeat makes the landing feel deliberate, and the slow tail lets the eye catch a row before the fade.

value.note: Hard cut at F137 (60 fps) from sentence one to a blank frame, then sentence two; the ground also shifts from #ffffff to #fcfefb. Missed because both are flat light grounds with dark type.

s003 at 4.483 s is not a boundary (was recorded as a retype to continuous, which left the cut in place; a reject removes it): it is the blurred shrink of the hero number inside the drop shot (F133-F140 at 30 fps). The real change is the text swap at 5.300 s.

evidence: visuals/a1/b04-shrink.jpg F265-F305 (one continuous decaying diff, no cut)

value.note: Text swap on the held orange ground: number replaced by the comparison line, at F317 (60 fps). Counted as a cut (text swap). Candidate 5.3 in shots.json.
Second text swap on orange, at F369 (60 fps). Counted as a cut (text swap). Candidate 6.17 in shots.json.
Hard cut from the prompt bar on white to the chat window on #f6f9f6 (source frame 601). Candidate 10.02 in shots.json.

Not a dissolve: the table fades to the empty light ground over F941-F957 (15.68-15.95 s), the ground holds empty F957-F965, then the centred sentence fades in word by word from F966 (16.10 s). A fade through the ground, cut placed where the ground is empty.
Real dissolve: the sentence fades out while the tiny wall of source chips fades in over it, F1035-F1051 (17.25-17.52 s); the wall then creeps and, from 18.30 s, pushes in to readable size.

Not a dissolve: the picked chip fades to the empty light ground F1273-F1292 (21.21-21.53 s), the ground holds two frames, then the mark cuts on at F1294 (21.557 s) and the wordmark at F1298 (21.633 s). Sound stops dead at 22.36 s (audio.json silence).
